title: Nathaniel J. Smith - Trio: Async concurrency for mere mortals - PyCon 2018
summary: Nathaniel J. Smith's PyCon 2018 talk introducing Trio, a Python concurrency library designed around usability and structured concurrency. He live-codes a problem and analyzes pitfalls in other async libraries.
why: Recommended as a clear introduction to structured concurrency and as an explanation of subtle asyncio bugs that Trio avoids.

quote.text: one of the best explanations I've seen about what subtle bugs are easy to make with asyncio
